item.title: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum: Bearing Witness — Guide
item.description: The Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum, at the southern end of the Peace Park, is one of the most important and affecting museums in the world. Extensively renewed in 2019, it presents the atomic bombing of 6 August 1945 not through statistics but through the human beings who lived and died that day: a child’s scorched tricycle, a stopped watch, tattered school uniforms, photographs of the ruined city and the personal testimonies of survivors, the hibakusha.

item.title: Nagasaki Peace Park — Guide
item.description: Nagasaki Peace Park, laid out on a hill near the hypocentre of the atomic bomb dropped on 9 August 1945, is the city’s foremost place of remembrance and its prayer for a world without nuclear weapons. At its heart stands the monumental Peace Statue, a ten-metre bronze figure whose raised right hand points to the threat of nuclear weapons and whose outstretched left hand symbolises peace. Nearby, the Fountain of Peace remembers victims who died desperate for water, and monuments donated by countries around the world line the grounds.
